clue.text: Relic I discovered in a rooftop crater

parts.note: the top of the word roof is its first letter, R

indicators.note: something discovered in a place was found inside it, so I goes within the crater word

parts.note: a chasm is a deep crater or gorge

explanation.surface: An old relic turns up inside a crater in someone's roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered in' puts I inside CHASM; A and R (the top of roof) go in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic of the past, such as an old-fashioned word or custom, is a survival from earlier times.

clue.text: Fat cello playing? This is for viola!

indicators.note: playing the letters means working them into a new arrangement, as a player works a tune

explanation.surface: Is a big cello being played? This music is meant for the viola!
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' shuffles the letters of FAT CELLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola music is written on the stave sign that puts middle C on the centre line, the sign named for the alto voice.

clue.text: See 1
Mummy's God transformed Nubia's black dog

indicators.note: transformed letters have been changed into a new shape and order

explanation.surface: An Egyptian deity changed a Nubian's black dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges NUBIAS; 'black dog' describes the god, who is shown as a black jackal or dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian god of embalming watched over mummification, so he is the god of mummies.

clue.text: Perverse pleasure in South African country having a dodgy referendum after scrapping borders

parts.note: Chad is a country in central Africa

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order
scrapping the borders of the word referendum drops its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes perverse pleasure in an African nation holding a rigged vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after scrapping borders' trims the vote word's first and last letters before 'dodgy' shuffles what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: This German loanword names the malicious joy felt at another person's misfortune.

clue.text: Camp site oddly in the style of golf

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word site

parts.note: a la, from French, means in the style of
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A camp site arranged, strangely, like a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War was given this name.

clue.text: The Alamo, USA, most of all a vital relay station

indicators.note: taking most of all three words keeps each one short of its final letter

explanation.surface: The Alamo was, for the USA, the most vital staging post of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of all' drops the last letter of THE, ALAMO and USA, leaving TH, ALAM and US.
explanation.definitionFit: This part of the brain passes sensory signals on to the cortex, acting as a relay station.

clue.text: Girl has yet to travel a very long way

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, ending up in a new order

explanation.surface: A girl still has a great distance to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to travel' rearranges GIRL HAS YET.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit is the distance light covers in a year, so many of them are an enormous distance.

clue.text: Ravel, go away

definitions.meaning: to ravel is to tangle, to tie up in snarls
a rude British dismissal telling someone to clear off

explanation.surface: A curt instruction: tangle things up and leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the composer, but it is the verb meaning tangle; the British phrase is a mildly rude way of saying get lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, become tied in tangles; idiomatically, a British put-down meaning clear off.

clue.text: Weapon caused the sad end of Robert the Bruce

indicators.note: sad here means sorry or pitiful, the letters left in a poor state and rearranged
end of picks the last letter of the word Robert

explanation.surface: A weapon brought about the unhappy death of Scotland's King Robert the Bruce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad' rearranges THE BRUCE; 'end of' Robert supplies the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval siege engine that hurled stones with a counterweighted arm was a weapon of war.

clue.text: Next clue needs this for a diarist's age

definitions.text: Next clue needs this for a diarist's age

parts.words: Next clue needs this for a diarist's age
parts.note: the next clue is 13, and Adrian Mole's famous diary has him aged thirteen and a fraction

explanation.walkthrough: Sue Townsend's comic novel is The Secret Diary of Adrian Mole, Aged 13 3/4; add the fraction to clue 13 and you have his age.
explanation.definitionFit: The fraction 3/4 written out in words is the amount added to thirteen in the diarist's title.

clue.text: Little time lost amongst all that apprehension

indicators.note: something lost has gone missing, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: a mo is a short moment, a little time

explanation.surface: Not much time is wasted amid all that anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes MO from AMONGST.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety or dread, a feeling of apprehension, is what this borrowed German word names.

clue.text: Green art evolved first sort of nursery

indicators.note: first places the word for sort ahead of the rearranged letters

parts.note: kind means sort or type

indicators.note: evolved letters have developed into a new form

explanation.surface: Eco-friendly art developed as the first kind of nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like a colour or eco label but is anagram fodder; 'first' sets the word for sort at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A school for very young children is a nursery school, the German term meaning children's garden.

clue.text: Devote one's car etc for recycling

indicators.note: material for recycling is broken down and remade, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Give over your car and other belongings to be recycled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for recycling' rearranges ONES CAR ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: To dedicate something solemnly, especially to a sacred purpose, is to devote it.

clue.text: Bordeaux's appealing twice about a sweet top wine

parts.note: in French, the language of Bordeaux, beau means handsome or appealing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the French pretty goes round the A

parts.note: a second French word for appealing is joli, pretty

indicators.note: the top of the word sweet is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Bordeaux drinker finds a sweet top-quality wine doubly attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' asks for a second French word for appealing; 'about' puts JOLI round A, and 'top' gives S from sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A light red from the Burgundy region of France is an example of a wine.

clue.text: Solo flight from German city is completed

indicators.note: a flight from a place is a departure, so Solo's name leaves the city

parts.note: Hanover is a city in northern Germany
Han Solo is the Star Wars pilot, so Solo stands for Han

explanation.surface: A solo flight leaving a German city is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight from' takes HAN (as in Han Solo) out of HANOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: When something has finished, such as a match or a lesson, it is said to be done, completed.

clue.text: 'e by gum, camping? Having covered skin

indicators.note: having covered means enclosing, so the camping word wraps round the others

parts.note: someone camping is in a tent
'e is a dialect spelling of he with the h dropped, giving just E
taken as written

explanation.surface: A northerner's exclamation about camping, with skin under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum' is a northern English exclamation of surprise. 'Having covered' puts E and GUM inside IN TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An outer protective layer, such as a skin, shell or husk, is called by this zoological term.

clue.text: Future is mine

definitions.meaning: a noun meaning outlook or chance of things to come
a verb meaning to search the ground for gold or ore

explanation.surface: Someone claims the future belongs to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the possessive, but it is the verb for digging for ore.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an expectation of the future; the other is to explore ground for minerals.

clue.text: A ruse deployed by Ottoman retreat round a pickle

indicators.note: deployed troops are spread into position, so these letters are rearranged
round means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round A
to retreat is to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Turk, member of the Ottoman Empire's people

explanation.surface: An Ottoman force's retreat after a ruse leaves them in a pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' shuffles A RUSE; 'retreat' reads the Ottoman word backwards, giving KRUT, and 'round' wraps it about the second A.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredded fermented cabbage is a kind of pickle, a German staple.

clue.text: Break item?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: loosening the other word's letters gives item

explanation.surface: A question about a fragment broken off something.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as anagram signal plus fodder, produces the clue word item.
explanation.definitionFit: A break from work or school is leisure, hours with no obligations.

clue.text: We rang about a rodent

indicators.note: about can mean around in disorder, signalling the letters are moved

explanation.surface: We telephoned about a rodent problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges WE RANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodents are named for gnawing, so a creature that chews constantly describes one.

clue.text: Angry with contemporary conflicting tendency

parts.note: cross means angry
current means present-day, contemporary

explanation.surface: Annoyed by the modern trend that cuts against everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a flow across the main stream; figuratively an opposing trend of opinion.

clue.text: See 19
Look here's ship entering port empty

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the ship goes between the remaining letters
empty takes the inside out of the word port, keeping its outside letters

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Pay attention: a ship is coming into an empty harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the outside of port, and 'entering' sets the steamship inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A whispered sound used to catch someone's attention, like saying hey, over here.

clue.text: Appearing shocked by deficit in part of hospital

indicators.note: in places the shortfall inside the hospital department

parts.note: A&E is the accident and emergency department of a British hospital
a gap is a shortfall, a deficit

explanation.surface: Someone looks stunned by a funding shortfall in a hospital department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E (accident and emergency) is the British casualty department; the ampersand is ignored. 'in' puts GAP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open-mouthed with wonder or surprise is staring in astonishment.

clue.text: Wild flower from the Guardian is spotted in Leeds, perhaps

indicators.note: spotted in means seen inside, so these letters go within the others
perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged differently

parts.note: a newspaper refers to itself editorially as we
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rare bloom from this newspaper has been seen in a Yorkshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England. 'perhaps' shuffles it to EDELS, and 'spotted in' puts the newspaper's editorial pronoun and 'is' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This white Alpine bloom grows wild in mountains and is the national flower of Austria.

clue.text: Substitute for 'taser' may be 'tazer', essentially

indicators.note: may be suggests the word could become something else, a rearrangement
essentially picks the essence, the central letter of the second word

explanation.surface: A spelling note: an alternative form of taser is tazer, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges TASER to ERSAT; 'essentially' takes Z, the middle of tazer. The surface's swap of one letter for another is itself a substitute.
explanation.definitionFit: This German loanword describes an inferior imitation used in place of the real thing.

clue.text: Greedily eating suet pudding? Nothing French in that!

indicators.note: in that places the French word inside the rearranged letters
suet in a pudding is mixed and remade, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone wolfing down suet pudding finds nothing French about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pudding' shuffles the suet to ESUT, and 'in that' puts the French word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal word meaning hungry or voracious, describing someone who eats gluttonously.
